sections.heading: Abstract
sections.text:
Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction (CO2RR) to valuable fuels is a promising approach to mitigate energy and environment problems, but controlling the reaction pathways and products remains challenging. Here, a novel Cu2O nanoparticle film is synthesized by square-wave (SW) electrochemical redox cycling of high purity Cu foils. The cathode afforded up to 98% Faradaic efficiency (FE) for CO2 electroreduction to nearly pure formate under 45 atm of CO2 in bicarbonate catholytes. When paired with a newly developed NiFe hydroxide-carbonate anode in KOH/borate anolyte, a two-electrode high-pressure electrolysis cell achieved a high energy conversion efficiency up to 55.8% stably for long-term formate production. While the highpressure condition drastically increased the solubility of CO2 to enhance CO2RR and suppress hydrogen evolution, Cu2O (111) oriented film was found important to afford near ~100% CO2 reduction to formate. The results have implications to CO2 reduction into a single liquid product with high energy conversion efficiency.

3 Intense utilization of fossil fuels in recent decades leads to continuous increases of CO2 level in atmosphere, causing serious environmental threats1. CO2RR driven by renewable energies is a promising approach to close carbon cycle and derive fuels from CO2. Formate is one of the valuable fuels coming from CO2RR, useful in fuel cells for direct electricity generation 2, 3. Sn4-6, Pb7, 8, and In9-11 based electrocatalysts are commonly used for CO2RR to formate. Cu-based electrocatalysts are well-known for producing hydrocarbons and alcohols12, 13 accompanied by hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), with formate of low FE14-21 and mixed in various liquid products that require separation treatments12. In aqueous CO2RR systems, competition with HER limits the FE of CO2 conversion. An effective way to improve the electrocatalytic performance is to increase the supplying of CO2 to cathodes. CO2RR occurs through active solvated/hydrated CO2 (aq) and H2CO3 species22, 23 that show increased concentrations in electrolytes under increasing CO2 partial pressures according to Henry’s law24. Thus, conducting CO2RR at higher CO2 pressure is promising to increase the active carbon species in electrolytes and improve the efficiency25-31. However, Cu-based electrocatalysts typically produce diverse CO2RR products without high selectivity under high pressures25, 27, 31, 32. Also, an unmet challenge under high pressure is the lack of efficient oxygen evolution (OER) using non-precious metal electrocatalyst to pair with CO2RR for high overall energy conversion efficiency. This work devised a SW electrochemical redox cycling treatment of ultrapure copper foil to produce sub-micron thick films rich in (111) oriented Cu2O nanoparticles anchored on Cu (denoted as SW-Cu2O/Cu) for CO2RR in a high-pressure electrolyzer under 1-60 atm CO2 partial pressures. In KHCO3 electrolytes at pressure above 45 atm, CO2RR with SW-Cu2O/Cu cathode dominated over HER, affording up to 98% FE for selective formate production. SW-Cu2O/Cu maintained a high formate selectivity over long-term (~20 h) CO2RR. Up to 55.8% energy efficiency was achieved for full-cell electrolysis when paired with NiFe hydroxide-carbonate OER catalyst33 in newly devised KOH/borate anolytes capable of maintaining basic pH environments under high CO2 pressures. The full electrolyzer led to energy efficient formate production of useful quantities (~0.4 g/cm2) without the need of product separation.

We synthesized SW-Cu2O/Cu films by SW treatment of 99.999% Cu foil in a concentrated KOH solution (pH 13.7) at 40 oC with 2.3 M lactate ions, through applying alternating oxidation and reduction potentials of -0.45 and -0.75 V vs. SCE reference electrode at 5 Hz over 0.5-10 h

Cyclic voltammetry (CV) showed two oxidation peaks and one reduction peak (Fig. 1b), corresponding to the Cu(0)→Cu(OH)2-→Cu2O/CuO→Cu(0) cycle34. Through the cycling a net oxidation > reduction charge was observed (Fig. S1a), which combined with mild etching to produce a rough Cu2O nanoparticles film in 0.5 h (Fig. 1c) with 200-300 nm thick (Fig. 1d) on Cu foil surface (Fig. 1e), and rich in (111) oriented planes based on X-ray diffraction (XRD) (Fig. 1f, S1d). Aberration corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) image of single particles on 0.5h-SW-Cu2O/Cu surface (Fig. 1g) and corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) pattern (Fig. 1h) clearly resolved (111) oriented planes.

CO2RR under high CO2 pressures. a, Schematic of the home-designed high-pressure CO2RR system. b, Calculation of active carbon species concentrations and pH in 0.5 M KHCO3 under different pressures at 25 oC. c, Current densities of 0.5h-SW-Cu2O/Cu in 0.5 M KHCO3 during 1 h CO2RR at -0.84 V vs. RHE under 1-60 atm. The current density decreased with pressure increasing from 1-45 atm, but remained unchanged from 45-60 atm. d, Product distributions of 1 h CO2RR under 1 atm at various potentials.
We performed three-electrode CO2RR in purified 0.5 M KHCO3 electrolytes saturated with 1-60 atm CO2 in a home-designed system (Fig. 2a) with Nafion membrane separating cathodic/anodic zones to prevent crossover of liquid reduction products. According to Henry’s law24 and dissolution equilibria of H2CO3, concentration of active CO2 (aq) and H2CO3 species in the electrolyte increased linearly with increasing CO2 partial pressure (Fig. 2b, S2). Calculation based on the concentration changes of these species showed a positive shift on the equilibrium potential of CO2 being reduced to formate (details in SI). Under CO2 pressures of 1, 25, 45, and 60 atm respectively, linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) revealed a decreasing trend in onset potentials under elevated CO2 pressures (Fig. S3), suggesting enhanced CO2RR.

7 Chronoamperometry measurements with SW-Cu2O/Cu cathode showed a decreasing trend of reduction current density under increasing CO2 partial pressures from 1-45 atm due to suppression of HER. The effect leveled off under 45-60 atm (Fig. 2c). At 1 atm, cathodic reduction was dominated by HER with FE of hydrogen formation >60%, and FE for CO2RR was lower than 30% (Fig. 2d). In strong contrast, electroreduction at 45 atm afforded a drastically suppressed HER FE to ~2.9% at -0.64 V vs. RHE. Formate was the dominant product under all overpotentials (Fig. 3a), with an FE reaching 97.7% under a partial current density of 5.2 mA/cm2 at -0.64 V. At more negative potentials than -1.04 V, formate FE decreased, with those of C2+ liquid products increased (Fig. 3a). Noted that the formate FE on SW-Cu2O/Cu cathode was much higher than on metallic Cu foil (~53%, Fig. S9b, S11) under a same CO2RR condition, indicating the importance of Cu2O for formate production. Under 60 atm CO2 pressure (Fig. 3b) at -0.64 V, the measured FE of CO2RR to formate was 98.2% with a partial current ~5.7 mA/cm2 while hydrogen was below the detection limit. At a higher current density of 26.6 mA/cm2 (i.e. -1.04 V), formate FE was still ~81.2% with barely any other liquid products generated. A maximum partial current density of 34.1 mA/cm2 for formate was achieved at -1.24 V with ~55.0% FE (Fig. 3c). Systematic investigations revealed a trend that HER FE decreased with increasing CO2 partial pressure at -0.64 V from ~64% at 1 atm to ~0% at 60 atm, accompanied by formate FE increasing from ~27% to ~98% (Fig. 3d, S5).

Previous density functional theory (DFT) simulations35, 36 suggested that the production of formate by CO2RR is favored over other products like CO on Cu2O (111) surface (details in SI). In a control experiment we performed SW treatment of Cu foil in a pH = 8 electrolyte and obtained a Cu2O nanoparticles film exhibiting more (100) oriented planes relative to (111) (Fig. S6b). The resulting cathode afforded ~87% FE of formate under 45 atm at -0.64 V over 30 min CO2RR (Fig. S6c), obviously lower than ~98% by SW-Cu2O/Cu enriched with (111). We also synthesized electrodeposited Cu2O/Cu with (111) and (100) orientations37, as well as directional growth Cu2O nanoparticle/C electrodes with (111) and (100) facets38 to further glean the importance of Cu2O

9 (111) surface to formate selectivity. At -0.64 V under 45 atm, both of the comparison showed higher formate FE with (111) dominated catalysts (Fig. S10). We observed that SW-Cu2O/Cu cathode exhibited slow phase changes through CO2RR (Fig. S4, S7). When extending CO2RR time to 20 h, the remaining Cu2O phase on surface decreased with formate FE decreasing accordingly. Nevertheless, reduction of SW-Cu2O/Cu was slow, with formate FE remaining as high as ~84% when only ~20% Cu2O was left after 20 h. During especially long-term CO2RR, the active electrocatalyst was a mixed phase of partially reduced Cu oxides, likely involving the interface of Cu2O and reduced Cu (Fig. S8, S11). We varied the SW treatment time from 0.5-10 h and found 5h-SW-Cu2O/Cu showing the highest Cu2O amount, with maximum ~84% formate FE (partial current density ~27 mA/cm2). We found the purity of copper is also an important factor. 0.5h-SW-Cu2O/Cu synthesized using 99.98% Cu foil afforded 67.9% formate FE at -0.64 V under 45 atm, much lower than ~97.7% afforded by cathodes using 99.999% Cu foil at the same condition (Fig. S9c). Among the impurities revealed by ICP-MS, Co was most likely causing higher HER FE and lower formate

sections.heading: FE.
sections.text:
SW-Cu2O/Cu operating at high CO2 pressures showed higher formate selectivity than previous Cu-based cathodes (Table S1), and compare favorably to known electrocatalysts for selective CO2RR to formate including In, Pb and Sn in terms of electrode area, partial current density or reaction duration/stability (Fig. S12-15, Table S2). We conclude that our Cu-based electrocatalysts can afford lower overpotentials for selective high-pressure CO2RR to formate, in addition to advantages of higher abundance and lower cost. High-pressure full-cell CO2RR with high energy conversion efficiency has been challenging and rarely tackled previously. We devised 2 M KOH + 0.8 M H3BO3 as a new anolyte for OER under high-pressure CO2 environments, with borate ions being unique in maintaining neutral or slightly basic anolyte pH. We monitored electrolyte pH by calibrating the shift of Ni(III)/Ni(II) redox peaks using Nernst equation (Fig. 4a) and found that 2 M KOH + 0.8 M H3BO3 anolyte pH was about neutral after equilibrating under high CO2 pressures (Fig. 4b), while 2 M KHCO3 catholyte was acidic (Fig. S16). We employed a non-precious metal based OER catalyst that were highly active and stable in neutral and slightly basic electrolytes, nickel-iron hydroxide carbonate (NiFe-HC)33 as the anode to pair with 5h-SW-Cu2O/Cu cathode for full-cell CO2RR-

OER electrolysis (Fig. 4c). Three-electrode CO2RR under 60 atm at -1.04 V vs. RHE using 5h-
SW-Cu2O/Cu cathode over 20 h showed a stable formate production with FE of ~80% and partial current density of ~26 mA/cm2 (Fig. 4d). Subsequently, two-electrode electrolysis cell with
separated anodic/cathodic zones was tested at 60 atm under constant current densities of 6 mA/cm2
and 30 mA/cm2 for 20 h respectively (Fig. S17-18). During the long-term 6 mA/cm2 electrolysis,
the full cell voltage stabilized at ~2.37 V with 92.7% formate FE (Fig. S17) and 55.8% energy
efficiency. For 30 mA/cm2 electrolysis, stable ~2.85 V was recorded with ~79.9% formate FE
(Fig. 4e) and 40.0% energy efficiency. These performances compared favorably over previous
reports (Table S3)39-43. We obtained a formate yield of ~20.6 mg/h/cm2 (0.412 g/cm2 in 20 h),
producing a useful amount of formate with >99.9% purity (molar ratio) among liquid products in
electrolytes. The novel two-electrode high-pressure electrolyzer opens up a new opportunity to
derive valuable liquid fuels from CO2.
